source_title: Inter and Milan unveil plans for new shared stadium to replace San Siro
source_excerpt:
Generali Stadium will have 71,500-seat capacity
Generali Stadium will have 71,500-seat capacity
Inter fans protest the plans outside gala event
Inter fans protest the plans outside gala event
Inter and Milan have unveiled plans for their new Generali Stadium, which will replace the shared San Siro venue from the 2031-32 season.
The stadium, sponsored by Generali – Italy’s largest insurance company – will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost the two clubs €1.2bn (£1bn). The plans were revealed at a gala event at Milan’s Castello Sforzesco on Thursday – but some fans in attendance voiced their opposition to San Siro being demolished.
Shortly before the briefing began, a group of Inter fans walked into the courtyard of the castle and unfurled a banner reading: “You will never extinguish the lights at San Siro,” and chanting: “Hands off San Siro.” Work on the new stadium is set to begin in 2028, on the site of the existing 75,000-capacity venue.
The Generali Stadium will be shaped “low in the body, and rises up at either end” behind the goals, the architect Norman Foster said. David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project, added that the steep-sided design aims to bring fans as close to the pitch as possible.
“The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that San Siro is a feeling,” Manica said. “It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling … we brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass.”
The stadium will also be capable of hosting NFL international games, rugby matches and concerts. Milan and Inter paid €197m to acquire the current San Siro stadium and its adjacent parking arenas. The current ground will be largely demolished once construction work nears completion.
Also known as the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, San Siro opened in 1926 and is the largest sports stadium in Italy. It is one of European football’s most famous venues, but requires extensive modernisation despite undergoing a number of renovations during its lifespan.
The Generali Stadium could be used as a venue for Euro 2032, which is being jointly hosted by Italy and Turkey. Foster and Manica previously worked together on the new Wembley Stadium, while the architect’s Foster + Partners firm also designed the plans for Manchester United’s proposed new 100,000-capacity home.
Additional reporting from Associated Press

hi_body:
इंटर मिलान और एसी मिलान ने आधिकारिक तौर पर अपने नए साझा स्टेडियम, 'जेनेरली स्टेडियम' की योजना पेश की है, जिसके 2031-32 सीज़न तक ऐतिहासिक सैन सिरो स्टेडियम की जगह लेने की उम्मीद है। इटली की प्रमुख बीमा कंपनी जेनेरली द्वारा प्रायोजित इस परियोजना की लागत लगभग 1.2 बिलियन यूरो होने का अनुमान है।

## परियोजना का विवरण और डिजाइन
* **क्षमता:** 71,500 सीटें।
* **डिजाइनर:** वास्तुकार नॉर्मन फोस्टर और स्टेडियम विशेषज्ञ डेविड मैनिका।
* **प्रस्तावित समयसीमा:** वर्तमान स्थल पर निर्माण कार्य 2028 में शुरू होने की संभावना है।

इस प्रस्तावित स्टेडियम का डिजाइन दर्शकों को मैदान के यथासंभव करीब रखने के लिए तैयार किया गया है। डेविड मैनिका ने कहा कि टीम का लक्ष्य पुराने स्टेडियम के माहौल को बनाए रखते हुए आधुनिक सुविधाएं प्रदान करना है। फुटबॉल के अलावा, इस स्टेडियम में रग्बी, एनएफएल मैच और संगीत कार्यक्रमों के आयोजन की भी योजना है।

## सार्वजनिक प्रतिक्रिया
मिलान के कास्तेलो स्फोरज़ेस्को में आयोजित कार्यक्रम के दौरान कुछ प्रशंसकों ने सैन सिरो को गिराने के फैसले का विरोध किया। प्रदर्शनकारियों ने बैनर लहराए और स्टेडियम के संरक्षण की मांग की, क्योंकि सैन सिरो का इतिहास 1926 से जुड़ा हुआ है।

## भविष्य की संभावनाएं
सैन सिरो, जिसे स्टेडियो ग्यूसेप मेज़ा के नाम से भी जाना जाता है, इटली का सबसे बड़ा स्टेडियम है। हालांकि इसमें कई बार नवीनीकरण हुआ है, लेकिन इसे आधुनिक जरूरतों के अनुसार ढालना एक बड़ी चुनौती है। अधिकारियों का मानना है कि नया जेनेरली स्टेडियम इटली और तुर्की द्वारा संयुक्त रूप से आयोजित किए जाने वाले यूरो 2032 के लिए एक स्थल के रूप में काम आ सकता है।

इन योजनाओं की पुष्टि दोनों क्लबों या मिलान शहर के आधिकारिक दस्तावेजों के माध्यम से की जा सकती है।

en_body:
Inter Milan and AC Milan have officially presented their proposal for a new shared venue, the Generali Stadium, which is slated to replace the historic San Siro by the 2031-32 season. The project, backed by Italian insurance giant Generali, is estimated to cost approximately €1.2 billion.

## Project Overview and Design
* **Capacity:** 71,500 seats.
* **Designers:** Architect Norman Foster and stadium specialist David Manica.
* **Expected Timeline:** Construction is scheduled to begin in 2028 on the current site.

The proposed structure features a unique design meant to keep fans as close to the pitch as possible. David Manica emphasized that the design team aimed to replicate the atmosphere of the current stadium while modernizing the experience. Beyond football, the venue is intended to host rugby, NFL international games, and major concerts.

## Community Reaction
The unveiling at Milan’s Castello Sforzesco was met with public dissent. Supporters gathered to protest the demolition of the existing San Siro, which opened in 1926. Demonstrators displayed banners and chanted slogans, highlighting concerns over losing a venue deeply rooted in football history.

## Future Prospects
The current San Siro, also known as the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, has undergone multiple renovations but faces ongoing challenges regarding its modernization. Officials suggest the new Generali Stadium could potentially serve as a venue for Euro 2032, a tournament to be co-hosted by Italy and Turkey. 

Verification of these plans can be confirmed via official statements from the two clubs or the City of Milan's urban planning records.
en_title: Inter and Milan Unveil Plans for New Shared Generali Stadium
